_note: One place for everything likely to change about reviewers: which models are tried per role, what a tag may name, what one review costs, the hard caps on a single review, quota kept back, and dated notes. How it is read, and how to change it, is docs/workflow.md -> Choosing a reviewer. Defaults are tried in order, first to last: the first that has a local CLI, enough usage, no reservation against it, and a working bubblewrap sandbox wins. Models here are the cheap end of what is allowed; the expensive ones are kept for sensitive work. Why each is here: docs/workflow.md and docs/research/reviewer-models-2026-11.md.
_note_zai: zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3 is the same GLM on the Z.ai coding-plan connector, which does not touch OpenCode Go quota. It needs that connector signed in on the runner (tools/runner-setup.md) and is not a default.

caps._note: Hard limits on one review, so a review can never take a large share of an allowance. Read by tools/agent-review.mjs; the table in docs/workflow.md explains each one.

notes.note: Pools differ inside one provider: Opus and Sonnet share Claude's weekly pool, Fable 5.2 has its own. Recheck when Claude's plans change.
On OpenCode Go, GLM-5.3 empties that allowance several times faster per review than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, so DeepSeek is the default and GLM goes through the Z.ai coding plan.

On Cursor, only its own models (Composer, Grok) come out of the weekly pool; Claude or GPT through Cursor bills prepaid credit at API list price from the first request. So only Composer 2.5 is allowed, and it has no token cap: its 480 s timeout is the whole limit.

opencode-go/glm-5.3 keeps a cost weight and a per-review share as the measured record, but it is not in allowed: a review must not be routed to it while a review there empties that allowance, so a tag naming it is refused and falls back to the role's default.

Claude's --max-budget-usd is a client-side estimate of API list prices, not the plan's own meter, so it is a guardrail beside the turn cap, not a promise about the subscription. --max-turns is real but hidden from --help in 2.1.x.
Codex has no turn or budget cap in exec mode; model_reasoning_effort and model_auto_compact_token_limit are the only levers, and turn.completed in --json reports the tokens used.
